html:
Pama-Nyungan is the largest family of Aboriginal Australian languages, with about 300 of the roughly 400 languages once spoken on the continent. It covers nearly all of mainland Australia except the far north.

The name joins two words for "man" at the two ends of its range: pama in the far northeast and nyungar in the far southwest. The languages are close enough to suggest a spread within the last several thousand years; one study traced the family to the Gulf country of Queensland about 6,000 years ago, though this is debated. The Western Desert language and Gamilaraay belong to it.

The other families, called non-Pama-Nyungan, are packed into the Kimberley and the Top End. Gooniyandi, Rembarrnga and Malak Malak belong to them. See also Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: Pama-Nyungan is the largest family of Aboriginal Australian languages, with about 300 of the roughly 400 languages once spoken on the continent. It covers nearly all of mainland Australia except the far north.
